result.title: Exact Distinguishability in Non-Markovian Decision Processes
result.comment: 26 pages, 7 figures. Code and Lean 4 proofs: https://github.com/Kcbir/pec
result.summary: Non-Markovian environments are often modeled as Regular Decision Processes (RDPs), where dynamics depend on the interaction history through a finite automaton. Existing offline guarantees for RDPs rely on a distinguishability assumption on the behaviour policy but provide no means of verifying it. When the assumption is violated, distinct models may explain the data equally well. We study when data collected under a fixed behaviour policy can distinguish two candidate RDPs. We prove that the posterior odds between observationally equivalent candidates remain equal to the prior odds at every sample size, even when the policy visits every automaton state, and verify both results formally in Lean 4. We then characterize this equivalence exactly and derive PEC, an algorithm that decides it in time linear in the size of the product automaton. The distinguishability assumption of prior work fails on three of our four test environments, and the experiment identified by PEC restores it in each case.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究非马尔可夫决策过程（RDP）中固定行为策略下数据能否区分两个候选模型，证明观测等价候选的后验几率恒等于先验几率，并以 Lean 4 形式化验证，进而给出线性时间的判定算法 PEC。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「历史依赖状态+可区分性判定」的概念可能启发 LVR 中隐状态是否真正影响答案、证据筛选与模型不可辨识性的刻画，可供核查但需较多迁移工作。
